stem: An agriculture study measures the yield per hectare (tonnes) for a sample of 15 farms. The sample mean is 11.1 tonnes with a sample standard deviation of 3.3 tonnes. However, 2 of the 15 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 13 observations have a mean of 10.4 tonnes and standard deviation of 2.6 tonnes. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 11.1, 95% CI = [9.3, 12.9]. Without outliers: mean = 10.4, 95% CI = [9.0, 11.8]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [9.0, 12.9]. Point estimate: 10.8 tonnes.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [9.0, 12.9].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
